This page connects textiles and soft goods to the same N.I.C.E., drawing, pattern, testing, feedback, and revision practices used elsewhere in design and fabrication.

## Core scope

- reading and creating patterns;
- grain, direction, stretch, and material behaviour;
- seam allowance and construction sequence;
- hand and machine sewing foundations;
- closures and fasteners;
- embroidery and heat-transfer processes;
- wearable, protective, storage, and other soft-goods design;
- fit prototypes, user testing, repair, and resource-efficient layout.

## Free pattern and textile resources

Generate customizable patterns with [FreeSewing](https://freesewing.eu/), draft parametric patterns with open-source [Seamly2D](https://github.com/FashionFreedom/Seamly2D), create embroidery files with [Ink/Stitch](https://inkstitch.org/), and compare documented builds through [Instructables sewing projects](https://www.instructables.com/craft/sewing/projects/). Always test fit, seam allowance, material behaviour, machine setup, and each pattern's licence. The [full free-resource directory · Work in Progress](../resources/work-in-progress/index.qmd) includes additional provisional learning and repair notes.
